newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bertrand Faure slumps on ECIA stake.
newsitem.headline: Bertrand Faure slumps on ECIA stake.

text.p: Shares in Bertrand Faure tumbled on Thursday after PSA Peugeot Citroen's car parts subsidiary ECIA took a 17 percent stake, effectively quashing the prospect of an outside takeover bid.
"A lot of people had bought Bertrand Faure for speculative reasons," a trader said.
The share was down seven francs, or four percent, at 178.10 at 0900 GMT, while the bourse index was down 0.7 percent.
ECIA said on Wednesday that it had acquired the stake by buying 75 percent of Financiere Michel Thierry in a transaction valuing the holding company at 578 million francs.

It said another equipment manufacturer, Treves, had acquired 25 percent of Financiere Michel Thierry, whose primary asset is the 17.3 percent stake in Bertrand Faure, which specialises in making car seats. Jointly, Ecia and Treves represent Bertrand Faure's biggest share grouping.
The newspaper Automotive News reported that Canada's Magna International Inc was eyeing Bertrand Faure to boost its seat-making capacity in Europe.
The PSA carmaking group has led a campaign to keep France's car parts making industry out of foreign hands, notably in the case of France's biggest components supplier Valeo.

"While the operation is strategically interesting for ECIA, it also ensures that Michel Thierry's large stake in Bertrand Faure remains in French hands," a Paris brokerage said in its daily stock comment.
The stake represents 25 percent of the voting rights.
Speculative interest in the car parts sector is based in large part on a rapid global consolidation of the industry.
Ecia said the acquisition of the Bertrand Faure stake was part of its strategy to increase its offerings of interior car equipment, a market expected to grow rapidly in coming years.
It said it had no plan to change the participation over the next week. Its shares were up sharply, gaining 40 francs at 649 in early trading.
PSA Peugeot Citroen shares were off 0.51 percent at 587.
